open_questions: One individual transit is shallow (151 ppm, -6.3 sigma) in 4 transits (share 0.3599) - follow-up transit photometry to confirm repeatable depth and rule out residual systematics.
Centroid inconclusive - ground-based photometry or high-resolution imaging to verify on-target location given no neighbour within 1 pixel.
xgb planet_rank 0.27 is below median (0.5) driven by transit scatter and depth change score - additional transits needed to test vs systematics.
dossier.public_summary: Signal is a ~13.9-day, ~2.1-Earth-radius dip with flat-ish shape, no odd/even difference and no secondary eclipse, on a nearby M dwarf with no plausible neighbour within a pixel. The large apparent change in depth between sectors matches only a change in TESS light-curve product (2-min vs standard SPOC) and is steady within each product, so the dip is still consistent with a planet. One shallow transit among four leaves a residual scatter that needs more observations to confirm, but a planet remains the best explanation.

reasons.why: Small, planet-sized (2.1 Rearth) from undiluted depth 764.5 ppm. No stellar sizes expected.
Odd/even depths 685.1 vs 818.2 ppm consistent (diff_ratio 1.2), no 2x-period binary.
No significant secondary (threshold 5, best brightening 2.898); phase 0.3572 not at 0.5.
No stars within one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) that could cause the dip; closest that could at 28.7 arcsec requires 0.2797 eclipse, ~3 sigma from target.

Apparent strong sector change (p_constant 3.777e-8, change 88.31%) is calibration between products: SPOC 2-min 1135 ppm err 90 steady (p_constant 0.213) vs TESS-SPOC 1-sector 467 ppm err 75, not a true depth change.
Centroid is inconclusive with no sector difference image, so no positive off-target localization; contratio 0.003142 is very low.

SNR high despite 4 transits with one outlier (depth 151 ppm vs mean 724 ppm, chi2 67.709); phase-curve small and not variable (chi2 19.65 dof 9); star density penalty 6.015 but duration ratio 1.4 within up to 1.5 central allowance.
